readings.title: What YeHoVaH Requires
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH pleads with His people, reminding them of His deliverance and declaring that He desires justice, loving-commitment, and humility over sacrifices.
readings.text: [Micah 6:1] Hear now what <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is saying, <dq>“Arise, strive with <dn>את</dn> the mountains, and let the hills hear <dn>את</dn> your voice.</dq> [2] <dq>“Hear, O you mountains, <dn>את</dn> the controversy of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and you everlasting foundations of the earth! For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has a controversy with <dn>His</dn> people and <dn>He</dn> shall reprove <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl.</dq> [3] <dq>“<dn>My</dn> people, what have <dn>I</dn> done to you? And how have <dn>I</dn> wearied you? Answer <dn>Me</dn>,</dq> [4] <dq>for <dn>I</dn> brought you up from the land of Mitsrayim, and <dn>I</dn> ransomed you from the house of bondage. And <dn>I</dn> sent <dn>את</dn> Mosheh, <dn>את</dn> Aharon, and <dn>את</dn> Miryam before you.</dq> [5] <dq>“<dn>My</dn> people, remember, please, <dn>את</dn> what Balaq sovereign of Mo’aḇ counselled, and <dn>את</dn> what Bil‛am son of Be‛or answered him, from Shittim to Gilgal, in order to know <dn>את</dn> the righteousness of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”</dq> [6] With what shall <dn>I</dn> come before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, bow <dn>myself</dn> before the high <dn>Elohim</dn>? Shall <dn>I</dn> come before <dn>Him</dn> with ascending offerings, with calves a year old? [7] Is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> pleased with thousands of rams or ten thousand rivers of oil? Shall <dn>I</dn> give <dn>my</dn> first-born for <dn>my</dn> transgression, the fruit of <dn>my</dn> body for the sin of <dn>my</dn> being? [8] <dn>He</dn> has declared to you, O man, what is good. And what does <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> require of you but to do right, and to love loving-commitment, and to walk humbly with <dn>את</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>?

readings.title: Judgment for Dishonesty
readings.subtitle: The voice of YeHoVaH cries out against the city's corruption, false measures, and violence, promising ruin for following the ways of Omri and Ahab.
readings.text: [Micah 6:9] The voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> cries to the city – and let sound wisdom see <dn>Your</dn> Name! <dq>“Hear <dn>את</dn> the Rod and <dn>Him</dn> who appointed it!</dq> [10] <dq>“Are there still treasures of wrongness in the house of the wrong, and the short measure that is an abomination?”</dq> [11] <dq>Would <dn>I</dn> be innocent with wrong scales, and with a bag of false weights?</dq> [12] <dq>“For her rich men are filled with cruel unrighteousness, and her inhabitants have spoken falsehood, and their tongue is deceit in their mouth.</dq> [13] <dq>“So <dn>I</dn> also, <dn>I</dn> shall strike you with a grievous wound, to lay you waste because of your sins:</dq> [14] <dq>“You shall eat but not be satisfied, and your inside be empty. And you shall store up but not save, and what you save <dn>I</dn> shall give to the sword.</dq> [15] <dq>“You shall sow but not reap, you shall tread <dn>את</dn> the olives but not anoint yourselves with oil, and make sweet wine but not drink wine.</dq> [16] <dq>“For <dn>את</dn> the laws of Omri are strictly observed, and all the works of the house of Aḥab, and you walk in their counsels. Therefore <dn>I</dn> give you for a ruin, and your inhabitants for a hissing, and let you bear <dn>את</dn> the reproach of <dn>My</dn> people.”</dq>

readings.title: The Prophet's Lament
readings.subtitle: Micah grieves the lack of righteousness and the prevalence of corruption, betrayal, and familial strife, yet resolves to look to YeHoVaH for deliverance.
readings.text: [Micah 7:1] Woe to me! For <dn>I</dn> am as gatherings of summer fruit, as gleanings of the grape harvest. There is no cluster to eat. <dn>My</dn> being has desired the first-ripe fruit. [2] The lovingly-committed one has perished from the earth, and there is no one straight among men. All of them lie in wait for blood, everyone hunts <dn>את</dn> his brother with a net. [3] Both hands are on the evil, to do it well. The prince asks for gifts, the judge seeks a bribe, and the great man speaks <dn>את</dn> the desire of his being. And they weave it together. [4] The best of them is like a prickly plant, the most straight is sharper than a thorn hedge. The day of your watchman and your punishment has come, now is their confusion. [5] Trust no friend, rely on no companion, guard <dn>את</dn> the doors of your mouth from her who lies in your bosom. [6] For son is despising father, daughter rises up against her mother, daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law, the enemies of a man are the men of his own house. [7] As for me, <dn>I</dn> look to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>I</dn> wait for the <dn>Elohim</dn> of <dn>my</dn> deliverance, <dn>my</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> does hear me.

readings.title: Confidence in YeHoVaH's Restoration
readings.subtitle: Despite present darkness and discipline, the prophet expresses confidence that YeHoVaH will plead his case, bring him into the light, and shame his enemies.
readings.text: [Micah 7:8] Do not rejoice over me, O <dn>my</dn> enemy. When <dn>I</dn> have fallen <dn>I</dn> have risen, when <dn>I</dn> sit in darkness <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is a light to me. [9] <dn>I</dn> bear <dn>את</dn> the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for <dn>I</dn> have sinned against <dn>Him</dn>, until <dn>He</dn> pleads <dn>my</dn> case, and shall execute right-ruling for me, until <dn>He</dn> brings me out into the light and <dn>I</dn> look on <dn>His</dn> righteousness. [10] And let <dn>my</dn> enemy see it, and let shame cover her who said to me, “Where is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>?” Let <dn>my</dn> eyes look on her: now she is trampled down like mud in the streets. [11] The day for building your walls! Let the law go far and wide in that day – [12] that day when they come to you from Ashshur and the besieged cities of Mitsrayim, and from the siege to the River, and from sea to sea, and mountain to mountain. [13] But the earth shall become a waste because of those who dwell in it, and for the fruit of their deeds.

readings.title: A Prayer for Mercy and a Song of Praise
readings.subtitle: A plea for YeHoVaH to shepherd His people as in days of old, culminating in praise for His unique compassion, forgiveness, and faithfulness to the covenants with Abraham and Jacob.
readings.text: [Micah 7:14] Shepherd <dn>Your</dn> people with <dn>Your</dn> rod, the flock of <dn>Your</dn> inheritance, who dwell alone in a forest, in the midst of Karmel. Let them feed in Bashan and Gil‛aḏ, as in days of old. [15] <dq>“As in the days when you came out of the land of Mitsrayim, <dn>I</dn> shall let him see wonders.”</dq> [16] Let the nations see and be ashamed of all their might, let them put their hand over their mouth, let their ears be deaf. [17] Let them lick <dn>את</dn> the dust like a serpent, let them come trembling from their strongholds like snakes of the earth, let them be afraid of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> and fear because of <dn>You</dn>. [18] Who is an <dn>Ěl</dn> like <dn>You</dn> – taking away crookedness and passing over the transgression of the remnant of <dn>His</dn> inheritance? <dn>He</dn> shall not retain <dn>His</dn> wrath forever, for <dn>He</dn> <dn>Himself</dn> delights in loving-commitment. [19] <dn>He</dn> shall turn back, <dn>He</dn> shall have compassion on us, <dn>He</dn> shall trample upon our crookednesses! And <dn>You</dn> throw all our sins into the depths of the sea! [20] <dn>You</dn> give truth to Ya‛aqoḇ, loving-commitment to Aḇraham, which <dn>You</dn> swore to our fathers from the days of old!

readings.title: Sennacherib's Invasion
readings.subtitle: In Hezekiah's fourteenth year, Sennacherib of Assyria captures Judah's walled cities. Hezekiah attempts to appease him with tribute, but the Assyrian king sends his commanders to Jerusalem.
readings.text: [2 Kings 18:13] And in the fourteenth year of Sovereign Ḥizqiyahu, Sanḥěriḇ sovereign of Ashshur came up against all the walled cities of Yehuḏah and captured them. [14] And Ḥizqiyah sovereign of Yehuḏah sent to the sovereign of Ashshur at Laḵish, saying, “<dn>I</dn> have done wrong, turn away from me. <dn>I</dn> shall bear <dn>את</dn> whatever you impose on me.” And the sovereign of Ashshur imposed upon Ḥizqiyah, the sovereign of Yehuḏah, three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold. [15] And Ḥizqiyah gave him all the silver that was found in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and in the treasuries of the sovereign’s house. [16] At that time Ḥizqiyah cut off <dn>את</dn> the doors of the Hěḵal of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>את</dn> the doorposts which Ḥizqiyah sovereign of Yehuḏah had overlaid, and gave it to the sovereign of Ashshur. [17] And the sovereign of Ashshur sent <dn>את</dn> the Tartan, and <dn>את</dn> the Raḇsaris, and <dn>את</dn> the Raḇshaqěh from Laḵish, with a great army against Yerushalayim, to Sovereign Ḥizqiyahu. And they went up and came to Yerushalayim. And when they had come up, they came and stood by the channel of the upper pool, which was on the highway to the Launderer’s Field. [18] And they called to the sovereign. And Elyaqim son of Ḥilqiyahu, who was over the household, and Sheḇnah the scribe, and Yo’aḥ son of Asaph, the recorder, came out to them.

readings.title: The Rabshakeh at the Upper Pool
readings.subtitle: Sennacherib sends the Rabshakeh with a great army to Jerusalem, where he is met by Hezekiah's officials.
readings.text: [Isaiah 36:1] And it came to be in the fourteenth year of Sovereign Ḥizqiyahu that Sanḥěriḇ sovereign of Ashshur came up against all the walled cities of Yehuḏah and took them. [2] And the sovereign of Ashshur sent <dn>את</dn> the Raḇshaqěh with a great army from Laḵish to Sovereign Ḥizqiyahu at Yerushalayim. And he stood by the channel of the upper pool, on the highway to the Launderer’s Field. [3] And there came to him Elyaqim son of Ḥilqiyahu, who was over the household, and Sheḇnah the scribe, and Yo’aḥ son of Asaph, the recorder.

readings.title: A Challenge to Hezekiah's Trust
readings.subtitle: The Rabshakeh mocks Hezekiah's reliance on Egypt and claims that YeHoVaH Himself commanded Assyria to attack Judah.
readings.text: [2 Kings 18:19] And the Raḇshaqěh said to them, “Please say to Ḥizqiyahu, ‘Thus said the great sovereign, the sovereign of Ashshur, “What is this trust in which you have trusted? [20] “You have spoken of having counsel and strength for battle, but they are only words of the lips! And in whom do you trust, that you rebel against me? [21] “Now look! You have put your trust in the staff of this crushed reed, Mitsrayim, on which if a man leans, it shall go into his hand and pierce it. So is Pharaoh sovereign of Mitsrayim to all who trust in him. [22] “But when you say to me, ‘We trust in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>,’ is it not <dn>He</dn> whose high places and whose slaughter-places Ḥizqiyahu has taken away, and said to Yehuḏah and Yerushalayim, ‘Bow yourselves before this slaughter-place in Yerushalayim’?” ’ [23] “And now, <dn>I</dn> urge you, give a pledge to <dn>my</dn> master the sovereign of Ashshur, then <dn>I</dn> give you two thousand horses, if you are able to put riders on them! [24] “And how do you turn back <dn>את</dn> the face of one commander of the least of <dn>my</dn> master’s servants, and trust in Mitsrayim for chariots and horsemen? [25] “Have <dn>I</dn> now come up without <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> against this place to destroy it? <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>‘Go up against this land, and you shall destroy it.’ ”</dq>’ ”

readings.title: A Message to the People of Jerusalem
readings.subtitle: Speaking in Hebrew, the Rabshakeh urges the people to surrender, promising prosperity and warning them not to trust in Hezekiah or YeHoVaH, who he claims is no different from the gods of other conquered nations.
readings.text: [2 Kings 18:26] Then said Elyaqim son of Ḥilqiyahu, and Sheḇnah, and Yo’aḥ to the Raḇshaqěh, “Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it. And do not speak to us in the language of Yehuḏah, in the ears of the people on the wall.” [27] And the Raḇshaqěh said to them, “Has <dn>my</dn> master sent me to your master and to you to speak <dn>את</dn> these words, and not to the men sitting on the wall to eat their own dung and drink their own urine, with you?” [28] And the Raḇshaqěh stood and called out with a loud voice in the language of Yehuḏah, and spoke and said, “Hear <dn>את</dn> the word of the great sovereign, the sovereign of Ashshur! [29] “Thus said the sovereign, ‘Do not let Ḥizqiyahu deceive you, for he is unable to deliver you out of his hand, [30] and do not let Ḥizqiyahu make you trust in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall certainly deliver us, and this city is not given into the hand of the sovereign of Ashshur.” ’ [31] “Do not listen to Ḥizqiyahu, for thus said the sovereign of Ashshur, ‘Make peace with me by a present and come out to me, and let each of you eat from his own vine and each from his own fig tree, and each of you drink the waters of his own cistern, [32] until <dn>I</dn> come. Then <dn>I</dn> shall take you away to a land like your own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive-trees and honey, and live, and not die. But do not listen to Ḥizqiyahu, when he misleads you, saying, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall deliver us.” [33] Has any of the mighty ones of the nations at all delivered <dn>את</dn> its land from the hand of the sovereign of Ashshur? [34] Where are the mighty ones of Ḥamath and Arpaḏ? Where are the mighty ones of Sepharvayim and Hěna and Ivvah? Did they deliver <dn>את</dn> Shomeron from <dn>my</dn> hand? [35] Who among all the mighty ones of the lands have delivered their land out of <dn>my</dn> hand, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> should deliver <dn>את</dn> Yerushalayim from <dn>my</dn> hand?’ ” [36] But the people were silent and did not answer him a word, for the command of the sovereign was, “Do not answer him.” [37] And Elyaqim son of Ḥilqiyah, who was over the household, and Sheḇnah the scribe, and Yo’aḥ son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Ḥizqiyahu with their garments torn, and they reported to him <dn>את</dn> the words of the Raḇshaqěh.

readings.title: The Assyrian Taunt
readings.subtitle: The Rabshakeh questions Judah's trust, belittling their reliance on Egypt and misinterpreting Hezekiah's reforms as an offense against YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [Isaiah 36:4] The Raḇshaqěh then said to them, “Please say to Ḥizqiyahu, ‘Thus said the great sovereign, the sovereign of Ashshur, “What trust is this in which you trust? [5] “<dn>I</dn> say: You speak of having counsel and strength for battle, but they are vain words. Now in whom do you trust, that you have rebelled against me? [6] “Look! You are trusting in the staff of this broken reed, Mitsrayim, on which if a man leans, it shall go into his hand and pierce it. So is Pharaoh the sovereign of Mitsrayim to all who trust in him. [7] “But if you say to me, ‘We trust in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>,’ is it not <dn>He</dn> whose high places and whose slaughter-places Ḥizqiyahu has taken away, and has said to Yehuḏah and to Yerushalayim, ‘Bow yourselves before this slaughter-place’? [8] “And now, <dn>I</dn> urge you, please give a pledge to <dn>my</dn> master the sovereign of Ashshur, and <dn>I</dn> give you two thousand horses, if you are able on your part to put riders on them! [9] “And how do you refuse one officer of the least of <dn>my</dn> master’s servants, and put your trust in Mitsrayim for chariots and horsemen? [10] “And now, have <dn>I</dn> come up without <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> against this land to destroy it? <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>‘Go up against this land, and destroy it.’ ”</dq>’ ”

readings.title: A Deceptive Offer of Peace
readings.subtitle: Ignoring the officials' request to speak in Aramaic, the Rabshakeh addresses the people on the wall directly, urging them to surrender and not to trust in YeHoVaH's power to deliver them.
readings.text: [Isaiah 36:11] And Elyaqim, Sheḇnah, and Yo’aḥ said to the Raḇshaqěh, “Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it. And do not speak to us in the language of Yehuḏah in the hearing of the people who are on the wall.” [12] But the Raḇshaqěh said, “Has <dn>my</dn> master sent me to your master and to you to speak <dn>את</dn> these words, and not to the men who sit on the wall, to eat their own dung and drink their own urine with you?” [13] And the Raḇshaqěh stood and called out with a loud voice in the language of Yehuḏah, and said, “Hear <dn>את</dn> the words of the great sovereign, the sovereign of Ashshur! [14] “Thus said the sovereign, ‘Do not let Ḥizqiyahu deceive you, for he is unable to deliver you, [15] and do not let Ḥizqiyahu make you trust in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall certainly deliver us, this city is not given into the hand of the sovereign of Ashshur.” ’ [16] “Do not listen to Ḥizqiyahu, for thus said the sovereign of Ashshur, ‘Make peace with me by a present and come out to me. And let each of you eat from his own vine and each from his own fig tree, and each of you drink the waters of his own cistern, [17] until <dn>I</dn> come. Then <dn>I</dn> shall take you away to a land like your own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards. [18] Beware lest Ḥizqiyahu mislead you, saying, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall deliver us.” Has any one of the mighty ones of the nations delivered <dn>את</dn> its land from the hand of the sovereign of Ashshur? [19] Where are the mighty ones of Ḥamath and Arpaḏ? Where are the mighty ones of Sepharvayim? And when have they delivered <dn>את</dn> Shomeron from <dn>my</dn> hand? [20] Who among all the mighty ones of these lands have delivered their land from <dn>my</dn> hand, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> should deliver <dn>את</dn> Yerushalayim from <dn>my</dn> hand?’ ” [21] But they were silent and answered him not a word, for the command of the sovereign was, “Do not answer him.” [22] And Elyaqim son of Ḥilqiyahu, who was over the household, Sheḇnah the scribe, and Yo’aḥ son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Ḥizqiyahu with their garments torn, and they reported to him <dn>את</dn> the words of the Raḇshaqěh.
